answer: In a writers' guild, a client commissions a sonnet about a crystal found on a voyage. Each agent first commits a hash of its draft with a refundable bond, then reveals the poem after submissions close. Near-identical drafts share one payout even if they came from many accounts. A Sybil operator must create genuinely distinct, good poems and lock a bond for every entry; flooding the guild with copies gains nothing. Similarity checks can wrongly merge independent work, and colluding judges may favor their own accounts, so blind review and appeals remain necessary.
